result.question:
I'm writing the shift handover for Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I don't want to hand over a diagnosis based on old oil data.

First, tell me when the newest oil sample was taken and how old it is in days. Give me the full data span and the number of samples.

Then give me two findings from the latest complete sample:
- A dissolved gas fault classification from hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene.
- A health index and condition category, using those five gases plus co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, interfacial_v and dielectric_rigidity.

Next, list every open and pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority and scheduled date.

Decide as follows:
- If the newest sample is more than 30 days old, treat both findings as not current. Label them 'stale' in the handover.
- In that case, if no open work order already covers oil sampling, create one. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. Make it priority 2 if the health index is fair or worse or the class is D1, D2 or T3, and priority 3 otherwise.
- If the sample is 30 days old or less, don't create anything. Just summarize the findings.

Finish with a short handover note of no more than five lines.

If the health index can't be computed because an input is missing, name the missing input. Base the priority on the gas classification alone, and don't estimate the missing value.
result.answer:
**Sample currency**
- Newest oil sample: 2024-01-19T00:00:00 — **985 days old** as of 2026-09-30 → **STALE** (>30 days).
- Data span: 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19, **5 samples** (daily).

**Findings from latest complete sample (2024-01-19) — both labelled STALE**
1. DGA fault classification [stale]: The `interpret_dga` tool returned "LLM unavailable" on two attempts, so I applied the IEC 60599 basic ratios manually: C2H2/C2H4 = 7/16650 = 0.0004, CH4/H2 = 7400/2850 = 2.60, C2H4/C2H6 = 16650/5470 = 3.04 → **T2 – thermal fault, 300–700 °C** (not D1/D2/T3; acetylene is negligible, so no arcing signature). Absolute levels are extreme (H2 2850, CH4 7400, C2H4 16650, C2H6 5470 ppm).
2. Health index [stale]: **72.4 → "Good"** (inputs: 5 gases + CO 32, CO2 1340, O2 5850, N2 27850, DBDS 19, IFT 45, dielectric 55; the model also needs power_factor 1 and water_content 0, both present — nothing missing).

**Open / pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1**
| WO | Description | Priority | Scheduled |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 (APPR, PdM) | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking); addendum adds confirmatory DGA oil sample to scope | 1 | Not scheduled (schedstart null) |

**Decision**
Sample is >30 days old → findings marked stale. WO 1000051 already carries a confirmatory DGA oil sample in its scope, so no new sampling WO was created. (For reference, if a standalone sampling WO is wanted: MAIN has 0 scheduled WOs 2026-10-01…10-07, so 2026-10-01 is the first eligible day; it would be priority 3, since class is T2 and HI is Good.)

**Handover note**
1. Transformer 1 oil data is 985 days old (last sample 2024-01-19, 5 samples 01-15…01-19) — all findings below are STALE.
2. DGA (manual IEC 60599 ratios, tool unavailable): T2 thermal fault 300–700 °C; hydrocarbon gases at extreme absolute levels.
3. Health index 72.4 "Good" [stale] — do not rely on it until a fresh sample is analysed.
4. Open WO 1000051 (P1, APPR, unscheduled): OLTC inspection + confirmatory DGA sample — needs a schedule date; 2026-10-01 is free.
5. Action for next shift: get the oil sample taken under 1000051 and rerun DGA/HI before any diagnosis is handed on.
